html:
The Paresi, who call themselves Halíti, are an Arawakan people of the Parecis plateau in Mato Grosso, Brazil.

They farmed manioc and maize in large villages. After gold was found near Cuiabá in 1719, during the Brazilian gold rush, slave raiders called bandeirantes captured many Paresi to work the mines. In the early 1900s the telegraph line of Cândido Rondon crossed their land, and many Paresi worked on it. Their relatives by language are the Enawenê-nawê, and the Nambikwara live to the west. Today soybean farms surround their reserves, and some Paresi farm soy themselves.
sum: The Paresi, who call themselves Halíti, are an Arawakan people of the Parecis plateau in Mato Grosso, Brazil.
